parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two services do belong to one concern: both deal with appointments, and AppointmentsController injects both of them. The problem is that they don't access data the same way. SchedulingService works through the persistence DAOs (PatientDao, AppointmentDao) and turns each row into a domain entity (Patient, Practitioner, Appointment). VisitNotesService skips that pattern. It uses the raw Prisma client (this.prisma.visitNote.create / findMany) directly, builds its own record id inline, and returns a plain VisitNote interface it declares itself instead of a domain entity. So the module uses two different data-access styles, and VisitNotesService goes around the DAO layer the rest of the module relies on. This is a question of which abstraction is used, not import direction, so it is in scope. A smaller issue: SchedulingService converts a stored row into an Appointment in two places (in book() and in cancel()) instead of doing it once.

violations.message: This file uses PrismaService (prisma.visitNote.create/findMany) directly and returns a VisitNote interface it declares itself. The other service in the module goes through DAOs (PatientDao, AppointmentDao) and domain entities, so this file skips that abstraction.
The row-to-Appointment conversion (new Appointment(a.id, ..., a.status as AppointmentStatus)) is written out in both book() and cancel() instead of being defined once.
